A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Chorus and retain matching methods, experiments, and figures. All essential material is readable. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v3 includes supplementary Sections A–E, allowing their newly included content to be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original Chorus segmentation, question-answering, probing, data-efficiency, adaptation, and ablation results in Tables 1–10 and associated figures.

after.justification: v3 retains original Chorus results and reports additional robustness experiments, teacher ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The core encoder, teachers, losses, augmentations, and rendering-based adaptation remain unchanged. However, v3 Appendix C.2 describes reducing the VLM task-guided sparsifier to one attention block, whereas both versions' Section 4.1 says components other than the backbone remain unchanged. This inconsistency prevents distinguishing an architectural revision from a newly disclosed implementation detail.

E1.justification: The datasets and principal tasks are retained. v3 extends evaluation to ScanNet++ iPhone RGB-D captures rather than only laser-derived point clouds, and adds tests on differently optimized Gaussian representations. These broaden input conditions within the existing indoor-scene coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in corresponding main experiments is unchanged. SceneSplat's retraining changes its settings and scores, not its method identity. The added analyses use existing comparators such as Sonata and SceneSplat; teacher combinations are method ablations.

E3.justification: v3 reports retraining the joint-data SceneSplat baseline using updated Matterport3D reconstructions, revising a comparison control. Added tests vary Gaussian optimization, density, and capture source, while Appendix D introduces DINO-first probing and a specified UMAP sampling protocol. The main benchmark metrics remain unchanged. Most appendix training budgets, splits, and processing settings are newly disclosed rather than established changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v3 adds optimization/density and iPhone robustness tests in Tables 10–11. The supplement adds DINO-first teacher ablations, visibility-crop analysis, UMAP comparisons, additional scene-feature examples, and before/after adaptation diagnostics. These substantially expand evidence about teacher contributions, input robustness, feature organization, and adaptation failures.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental error bars. The added pose-sampling averages describe data characteristics, not uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces SceneSplat's joint-training scores: ScanNet200 f-mIoU/f-mAcc changes from 21.4/38.7 to 22.5/41.7, while Chorus remains 24.6/47.7. These accompany revised baseline training, not a same-setting Chorus improvement. v3 also adds substantial results in Tables 10–11 and C, including iPhone scores of 45.7/57.6 for Chorus versus 39.5/52.0 for Sonata, plus new qualitative findings. Most retained main results are unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 motivates the augmentations qualitatively and refers to unavailable supplementary equations. v3 Appendix A.3 supplies a Taylor-expansion and covariance argument for rendering-equivalent perturbations, and a projection/Fourier derivation relating scale inflation to Gaussian blur. These add substantive mathematical justification beyond notation changes or standard metric formulas.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain multi-teacher 3DGS pretraining, transferable and data-efficient scene embeddings, and rendering-based adaptation. Adding Q&A to the abstract restates a capability already claimed and evaluated in v1. The introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds a localized explanation of teacher compatibility through shared representations, separate projectors, and PHI-S balancing. It interprets the new robustness tests and explicitly discusses lamp/ceiling confusion and blurred boundaries after low-resolution adaptation in Appendix D.4. The existing point-cloud transfer hypotheses and offline pseudo-label-cost limitation remain.

D1.justification: The new supplement documents augmentation parameters, camera selection and cropping, teacher feature resolutions, Matterport3D reconstruction, InteriorGS label assignment and splits, prediction transfer, and downstream training settings. It specifies VLM optimization and two-H200 training hardware, among other details absent from v1. The abstract also replaces a future code/model-release promise with a linked code-release statement; repository availability is not independently established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including Occam's LGS, SAM 2, UMAP, OPT, evaluation metrics, Rosetta Neurons, and the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. The latter two support a new discussion of shared representations across teachers. The principal positioning relative to SceneSplat, point-cloud pretraining, and multi-teacher distillation is retained.

P1.justification: v3 expands brief descriptions and references to supplementary material into organized, step-by-step explanations of adaptation, augmentation, dataset construction, and evaluation, with a contents list and Sections A–E. This substantially changes the explanatory structure. The main narrative order remains stable, alongside grammar, terminology, notation, affiliation, and acknowledgement edits.

P2.justification: v3 adds robustness Tables 10–11, supplementary Tables A–C, Algorithm 1, and Figures A–I covering pipelines, data processing, and feature analyses. The expanded PCA gallery includes a reused main-paper example alongside additional scenes. Existing main figures are largely retained; Figure 6 moves, Table 4 gains an explanatory caption, and the runtime table becomes Table 12.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves an important documentation deficiency: v1 repeatedly refers to supplementary method equations and implementation details absent from the supplied PDF. The added derivations, data-processing instructions, training details, robustness tests, and failure analysis substantially strengthen reproducibility and evidential support. Documented SceneSplat retraining also improves comparison transparency. The unresolved VLM connector inconsistency limits clarity but does not outweigh these gains.
